passage:
I was third in the line at the bakery counter when I saw it. A man walked up and stood at the front, right beside the register. A woman in a green scarf, Gargi, turned to him with a smile and said, “Sorry to jump in, but the queue begins over by the door.”
He frowned. “I’m only buying one thing.”
“Of course,” she said, still pleasant. “Most of us are, though. It’s just past the door.”
For a second I thought he would snap. Instead he shrugged, muttered something, and walked to the end. Gargi turned back to the counter and did not look smug. I’m Sharmila, and I’m not sure whether she was nervous, but her voice never rose.

qa.q: What did Gargi say to the man at the front?
qa.a: Gargi said, “Sorry to jump in, but the queue begins over by the door.”

qa.q: What might Gargi have been feeling as she spoke to the man?
qa.a: Gargi may have felt a little nervous but determined to be fair, though Sharmila cannot know for sure; the passage only shows a pleasant, steady voice that never rose.

qa.q: What helped Gargi's request work, according to what Sharmila saw?
qa.a: Gargi smiled, stayed pleasant and repeated the point with no heat. She also did not gloat once the man had walked to the end.

qa.q: How might the man have experienced being sent to the end of the queue?
qa.a: He may have felt embarrassed or defensive at being pointed out, which fits his frown and excuse, but the pleasant tone let him shrug and walk to the end without a scene.

grounding: Shows an observer describing a woman politely saying where the line starts, with calm friendly firmness that works.

passage:
Tuesday, post office. Kamal was fifth in the line when a man stepped up to the window ahead of everyone. “Hi, the queue starts by the door,” Kamal said, smiling. The man nodded, said “Oh, sorry,” and went to the end.
Friday. Another man pushed in. Kamal repeated the same words. This time the man snapped, “Who made you the boss?” The woman ahead of Kamal went quiet, and the others looked away. Kamal’s heart thumped. He said, “Fair enough,” shrugged, and let it go rather than arguing.
Next Monday. Vinita, who had slid in near the front, saw Kamal glance at her. “Sorry, I didn’t see the line,” she said, and stepped back.

qa.q: Which day did the second man snap at Kamal?
qa.a: The second man snapped at Kamal on Friday.

qa.q: What was Kamal probably feeling when his heart thumped on Friday?
qa.a: Kamal was likely nervous and unsure, since the man turned hostile and no one spoke up. His quick, calm reply suggests he did not want the moment to grow into a fight.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Kamal to let it go on Friday?
qa.a: The man had turned hostile, and pushing further could have made things worse. Kamal had already said the line clearly, and it was not worth a quarrel.

qa.q: How might Vinita have felt when Kamal glanced at her on Monday?
qa.a: Vinita may have felt caught out and slightly embarrassed, which is why she apologised and stepped back at once.

grounding: Shows a person calmly saying where the line starts over several days, succeeding when friendly and letting it go when a man turns hostile.
